questions.question: Which is the highest mountain above sea level in the world?
questions.explanation: Everest is on the border of Nepal and China. It is about 8,800 metres high.

questions.question: Which river flows through the city of Paris?
questions.explanation: Many famous sights, such as Notre-Dame, stand right next to the Seine.

questions.question: Which river flows through London?
questions.explanation: Tower Bridge crosses the Thames, and tourist boats sail up and down it.

questions.question: Mont Blanc, or 'White Mountain', is a very high peak in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Mont Blanc stands on the border of France and Italy. It is the highest mountain in the Alps.

questions.question: Which huge hot desert covers much of North Africa?
questions.explanation: Parts of the Sahara have huge sand dunes. Other parts are rock and gravel.

questions.question: Niagara Falls is a huge waterfall on the border between Canada and which other country?
questions.explanation: The Niagara River carries water from Lake Erie over the falls and on to Lake Ontario.

questions.question: In which country is Mount Fuji, a volcano with a snowy top?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji is the highest mountain in Japan, at about 3,800 metres.

questions.question: Which famous river flows through Egypt and the city of Cairo?
questions.explanation: The ancient Egyptians grew their food on the fertile land beside the Nile.

questions.question: The Amazon River and its huge rainforest are on which continent?
questions.explanation: The Amazon carries more water to the sea than any other river.

questions.question: On which continent is Mount Kilimanjaro, a giant volcano close to the equator?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro is a volcano in Tanzania. It is the highest mountain in Africa.

questions.question: Which very salty lake lets people float easily on the water?
questions.explanation: The salt makes the water heavy, so people float on top of it.

questions.question: In which country is Loch Ness, a deep lake with a famous legend about a monster?
questions.explanation: People say a monster nicknamed Nessie lives in the deep, dark water.

questions.question: Which long mountain range runs along the west coast of South America?
questions.explanation: The Andes run through seven countries, from Venezuela in the north to Argentina and Chile in the south.

questions.question: The Rocky Mountains are on which continent?
questions.explanation: The Rockies stretch from Canada down through the USA.

questions.question: In old Greek stories, the gods lived on which mountain?
questions.explanation: Mount Olympus is a real mountain in Greece. It is about 2,900 metres high.

questions.question: What do we call the place where a river starts?
questions.explanation: Many rivers start high in the mountains as tiny streams. The end of a river, where it meets the sea, is its mouth.

questions.question: Mount Etna is a big volcano on which Italian island?
questions.explanation: Etna erupts often and has snow on top in winter.

questions.question: Which giant waterfall in Africa is named after a British queen?
questions.explanation: Local people call it 'the smoke that thunders', because the spray rises high into the air.

questions.question: What do we call a huge, slow-moving river of ice on a mountain?
questions.explanation: Glaciers move only a little each day. As they move, they grind the rock and carve out deep valleys.

questions.question: Finland is known as the land of thousands of what?
questions.explanation: Finland has well over a hundred thousand lakes. Many Finns have a little cabin by one.

questions.question: On which continent is the Gobi Desert?
questions.explanation: The Gobi lies in Mongolia and China. Its summers can be hot, but its winters are freezing cold.

questions.question: Which river flows through the city of Rome?
questions.explanation: Rome was built beside the Tiber, not far from the sea.

questions.question: The Pyrenees mountains form a border between France and which country?
questions.explanation: The tiny country of Andorra lies high in the Pyrenees.

questions.question: What do we call fast, rough water in a river, where it flows over rocks?
questions.explanation: Some people go rafting or canoeing on rapids for fun.

questions.question: What do we call a big area of land with very little rain?
questions.explanation: Deserts can be hot, like the Sahara, or cold, like the Gobi.

questions.question: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Himalaya means 'home of snow' in Sanskrit, an old language of India.

questions.question: Which big river starts in the Swiss Alps and flows through Germany to the North Sea?
questions.explanation: Many castles stand on the hills beside the Rhine.

questions.question: Into which ocean does the Amazon River flow?
questions.explanation: At its mouth the Amazon is many kilometres wide.

questions.question: The Ganges is a big river in which country?
questions.explanation: The Ganges starts in the Himalayas and flows through India into Bangladesh.

questions.question: The Yangtze is a very long river in which country?
questions.explanation: The Yangtze flows into the East China Sea near the big city of Shanghai.

questions.question: In which country is the Black Forest, a hilly area with many fir trees?
questions.explanation: The Black Forest is famous for cuckoo clocks and for a chocolate cake with cherries.

questions.question: Which famous mountain lies on the border of Switzerland and Italy?
questions.explanation: The Matterhorn is part of the Alps and is shaped like a sharp pyramid.

questions.question: What do we call the very top of a mountain?
questions.explanation: Climbers cheer when they reach the summit. The bottom of a mountain is called its foot.

questions.question: What do we call a large area of fresh water with land all around it?
questions.explanation: A river often flows into a lake or out of it.

questions.question: Lake Victoria is a huge lake on which continent?
questions.explanation: The River Nile flows out of this lake on its long journey north to Egypt.

questions.question: Why is it hard to breathe at the top of very high mountains?
questions.explanation: The higher you go, the thinner the air gets. Some climbers on Everest use extra oxygen.

questions.question: What do we call the big hills of sand that the wind builds in a desert?
questions.explanation: Wind can move dunes slowly across the desert. Some dunes are higher than a tall building.

questions.question: What do we call a place in a desert where there is water and plants can grow?
questions.explanation: Travellers and animals can drink at an oasis. Many have palm trees.

questions.question: Which long river flows from north to south through the middle of the USA?
questions.explanation: Its name comes from an old Native American word that means 'great river'.

questions.question: Which river flows through both Vienna and Budapest?
questions.explanation: The Danube also flows through Bratislava and Belgrade, so it links four capital cities.

questions.question: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?
questions.explanation: The river has cut into the rock for millions of years, and the layers show Earth's history.

questions.question: In which country is Angel Falls, a waterfall almost 1,000 metres high?
questions.explanation: It is often called the highest waterfall in the world. It is named after Jimmie Angel, an American pilot who flew over it in the 1930s.

questions.question: Iguazu Falls, a huge set of waterfalls, lies on the border of Argentina and which other country?
questions.explanation: The falls lie in a rainforest. Depending on how much water there is, they are made up of about 150 to 300 separate waterfalls.

questions.question: Which country has most of the Ural Mountains?
questions.explanation: The Urals run from north to south and are often seen as part of the border between Europe and Asia.

questions.question: In 1883 the volcano Krakatoa exploded. In which country is it?
questions.explanation: The sound of the explosion was heard thousands of kilometres away.

questions.question: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in the United Kingdom. Which part of the UK is it in?
questions.explanation: Ben Nevis is 1,345 metres high.

questions.question: Lake Geneva lies between Switzerland and which other country?
questions.explanation: Cities such as Geneva and Lausanne stand on its shore.

questions.question: Which desert on the Pacific coast of South America is one of the driest places on Earth?
questions.explanation: In some parts of the Atacama, rain almost never falls.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in Denmark?
questions.explanation: The Gudenå flows through Jutland, past Silkeborg and Randers.

questions.question: How many Great Lakes are there in North America?
questions.explanation: The lakes are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario. Canada and the USA share most of them.

questions.question: Which river flows through the Czech city of Prague?
questions.explanation: The famous Charles Bridge crosses the Vltava.

questions.question: Which river flows through St Petersburg in Russia?
questions.explanation: The Neva is short, but it is wide and deep, and the city has many bridges over it.

questions.question: Which river crosses the equator twice as it flows through the rainforest of Central Africa?
questions.explanation: Two countries, the Republic of the Congo and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, are named after it.

questions.question: The Dolomites, mountains with pale rock, are in which country?
questions.explanation: Their pale rock glows pink and orange in the evening sun.

questions.question: The word 'geyser' comes from the name of a famous hot spring in which country?
questions.explanation: The Icelandic name Geysir comes from a word that means 'to gush'.

questions.question: Lake Titicaca lies high in the Andes, between Peru and which other country?
questions.explanation: The lake lies about 3,800 metres above sea level.

questions.question: The ancient region of Mesopotamia lay between which two rivers?
questions.explanation: Mesopotamia means 'between the rivers' in Greek. Early cities such as Babylon grew there.

questions.question: Into which sea does the River Danube flow?
questions.explanation: Where it meets the sea, the Danube forms a big delta full of birds.

questions.question: Which river flows through the German port city of Hamburg?
questions.explanation: The Elbe flows into the North Sea and is a busy route for ships.

questions.question: Which river flows through Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam?
questions.explanation: The Mekong starts high on the Tibetan Plateau in China and ends in a big delta in Vietnam.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in Australia?
questions.explanation: The Murray flows through the south-east of Australia and reaches the sea in South Australia.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in Ireland?
questions.explanation: The Shannon flows through several lakes before it reaches the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: Which mountain is the highest in Germany?
questions.explanation: The summit is on the border with Austria. You can reach it by cable car.

questions.question: Which mountain range runs like a backbone down the length of Italy?
questions.explanation: The Alps are in the far north of Italy, but the Apennines run down the whole country.

questions.question: In which part of Africa are the Atlas Mountains?
questions.explanation: They run through Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

questions.question: Snowdon is the highest mountain in which country?
questions.explanation: Its Welsh name is Yr Wyddfa. You can walk up it, or take a small mountain train from the village of Llanberis.

questions.question: What do we call the fan-shaped area of land where a river splits up before it reaches the sea?
questions.explanation: The name comes from the Greek letter delta, which looks like a triangle.

questions.question: What do we call a small river that flows into a bigger river?
questions.explanation: The Moselle is a tributary of the Rhine.

questions.question: What do we call a big, winding bend in a river?
questions.explanation: The word comes from the Maeander, a very twisty river in Turkey.

questions.question: Himmelbjerget is a famous Danish hill. In which part of Denmark is it?
questions.explanation: It is about 147 metres high and was once believed to be the highest point in Denmark.

questions.question: What is Råbjerg Mile, near Skagen in Denmark?
questions.explanation: The wind pushes the dune about 15 metres every year.

questions.question: Which is the largest lake in Sweden?
questions.explanation: The Göta River flows out of Vänern to the sea near Gothenburg.

questions.question: Which desert covers most of Botswana?
questions.explanation: The San people have lived in the Kalahari for thousands of years.

questions.question: Why is China's Yellow River yellow-brown?
questions.correct: It carries a lot of fine yellow soil
wrong: There is gold in the riverbed
questions.explanation: The soil, called loess, washes into the river from the land it crosses.

questions.question: A mountain's height is usually measured from which level?
questions.explanation: That is why we say a mountain is 'so many metres above sea level'.

questions.question: Mount Pinatubo, which erupted strongly in 1991, is in which country?
questions.explanation: The gas and dust it threw high into the sky cooled the whole Earth a little for a year or two.

questions.question: Which river gave its name to India?
questions.explanation: The Indus starts in Tibet and flows mostly through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: Which river flows through both Warsaw and Kraków?
questions.explanation: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland. It flows into the Baltic Sea.

questions.question: Which river flows from the Alps through Geneva and Lyon to the Mediterranean?
questions.explanation: In Lyon the Rhône is joined by the Saône. Near the sea it splits up and forms a delta called the Camargue.

questions.question: Which lake in Siberia is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal holds about a fifth of all the unfrozen fresh water on the surface of the Earth.

questions.question: The Volga, Europe's longest river, flows into which sea?
questions.explanation: The Caspian is the largest inland body of water in the world. It has no outlet to the ocean.

questions.question: Denali is the highest mountain on which continent?
questions.explanation: Denali, also called Mount McKinley, is in Alaska. Its name comes from a local Native word that means 'the high one'.

questions.question: Aconcagua, the highest mountain in South America, lies in which country?
questions.explanation: At almost 7,000 metres, Aconcagua is the highest mountain outside Asia.

questions.question: Mount Kosciuszko, the highest mountain on the Australian mainland, is in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: A Polish explorer named it after the Polish hero Tadeusz Kościuszko.

questions.question: Aoraki is the Māori name of which mountain, the highest in New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Mount Cook is in the Southern Alps, on the South Island.

questions.question: Galdhøpiggen is the highest mountain in Scandinavia. In which country is it?
questions.explanation: It is in the Jotunheimen mountains and is about 2,470 metres high.

questions.question: Carrauntoohil is the highest mountain in which country?
questions.explanation: It is about 1,040 metres high and lies in County Kerry, in a range called MacGillycuddy's Reeks.

questions.question: Which Italian island volcano is called the 'Lighthouse of the Mediterranean' because it erupts again and again?
questions.explanation: Stromboli has erupted in small bursts for a very long time, so sailors could see it glow at night.

questions.question: Which mountain range curves through Slovakia, Poland, Ukraine and Romania?
questions.explanation: Transylvania, home of the Dracula legend, lies inside the curve of the Carpathians.

questions.question: The Brenner Pass is a famous route through the Alps between Austria and which country?
questions.explanation: It is one of the lowest passes across the main ridge of the Alps, so it has been used for centuries.

questions.question: Most of the Danube Delta, a huge wetland full of birds, lies in which country?
questions.explanation: A small part of the delta is in Ukraine.

questions.question: Which huge lake was formed behind the Aswan High Dam in Egypt?
questions.explanation: It is named after Egypt's leader in the 1950s and 1960s, and it stretches into Sudan.

questions.question: The Blue Nile begins in which country?
questions.explanation: The Blue Nile flows out of Lake Tana. It meets the White Nile in Sudan.

questions.question: Lake Constance borders Germany, Switzerland and which other country?
questions.explanation: The Rhine flows into the lake at one end and out of it again at the other.

questions.question: In which country is Lake Balaton, a large, shallow lake that is popular for summer holidays?
questions.explanation: Balaton is often called the largest lake in Central Europe. Its shallow water warms up quickly in summer.

questions.question: Which is the largest natural lake in England?
questions.explanation: Windermere lies in the Lake District in north-west England.

questions.question: Which is the largest lake in Finland?
questions.explanation: Saimaa is a maze of islands and inlets. It is home to a rare freshwater seal.

questions.question: Which is the largest glacier in Iceland?
questions.explanation: Several volcanoes lie hidden under the ice of Vatnajökull, which gives its name to a national park.

questions.question: The Aletsch Glacier, the longest glacier in the Alps, lies in which country?
questions.explanation: It lies in the Bernese Alps, below the Jungfrau, and is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: The Rhine Falls near Schaffhausen are among the biggest waterfalls in Europe by water flow. In which country are they?
questions.explanation: The falls are not very tall, but a huge amount of water goes over them every second.

questions.question: What do we call a curved lake left behind when a river cuts off one of its bends?
questions.explanation: The name comes from the U-shaped wooden collar used with oxen.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in France?
questions.explanation: Many famous castles stand along the Loire.

questions.question: Which river is the longest in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: The Severn starts in Wales, flows through England and ends in the Bristol Channel.

questions.question: Which big river flows through Venezuela and into the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Orinoco forms part of the border between Venezuela and Colombia.

questions.question: Which West African river flows through the cities of Bamako and Niamey?
questions.explanation: Two countries, Niger and Nigeria, are named after this river. It makes a huge bend through West Africa and ends in a big delta.

questions.question: The Thar Desert lies in north-west India and which other country?
questions.explanation: The Thar is also called the Great Indian Desert.

questions.question: Which desert fills the Tarim Basin in western China?
questions.explanation: Old Silk Road trade routes went around the edges of this desert.

questions.question: Which Icelandic volcano's ash cloud stopped many flights over Europe in 2010?
questions.explanation: The ash was a danger to aeroplane engines, so airspace was closed for several days.

questions.question: Cotopaxi, one of the highest active volcanoes in the world, is in which country?
questions.explanation: Cotopaxi has a snow cap even though it lies close to the equator.

questions.question: The Grossglockner is the highest mountain in which country?
questions.explanation: It is part of the Hohe Tauern range in the Alps.

questions.question: Which of the Great Lakes has the largest surface area?
questions.explanation: Superior is also the deepest of the five lakes, and it is often called the largest freshwater lake in the world by area.

questions.question: Which river flows through the city of Kyiv?
questions.explanation: The Dnieper flows from Russia through Belarus and Ukraine to the Black Sea.

questions.question: Which river reaches the Atlantic Ocean at Lisbon?
questions.explanation: The Tagus is the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula.

questions.question: Which river flows through the French city of Bordeaux?
questions.explanation: The Garonne starts in the Pyrenees and flows to the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: Which river flows through the Italian city of Florence?
questions.explanation: The Ponte Vecchio, a bridge with shops on it, crosses the Arno.

questions.question: Triglav is the highest mountain in which country?
questions.explanation: Its name means 'three heads'.

questions.question: The High Tatras mountains lie on the border between Poland and which other country?
questions.explanation: The Tatras are the highest part of the Carpathian Mountains.

questions.question: In which country is the Salar de Uyuni, the largest salt flat in the world?
questions.explanation: After rain, the thin layer of water turns the salt flat into a giant mirror of the sky.

questions.question: In which country does the Okavango River end in a huge inland delta instead of reaching the sea?
questions.explanation: The delta lies in the Kalahari and is full of wildlife, including elephants and hippos.
